title: The Record Must Tell the Truth

intelligence.essence: The record is the system's memory of itself, and every rule in this family exists because the record once lied politely. A mechanical change is still a change: a bulk sweep announced as "verified, tests passing" carried a syntax error that stopped the suite from even collecting — verdicts are bound to the exact bytes they were earned on, and no verdict crosses a commit, however trivial the commit claims to be. A skip is a verdict that must be earned per failure: of 26 failures, 21 were genuinely unsupported and skipped with reasons, one was a real defect that a blanket skip would have buried. When a failure appears, check the system before the seat: a repository teaching two incompatible truths at once manufactures seat errors wholesale, and the fix belongs to the system that taught wrong. Register at ingest time: seeds that outrun registration become an unregistered backlog that fails CI, loses identities, and costs more to reconcile than registration ever would. A note is not live when it is written — it is live when it is on main, synced, and clicked by its own author. Before building a new instrument, exhaust the existing one: most proof gaps are unasked questions of tools already in hand. Capture receipts are audited nightly, because intelligence that leaks into chat history is intelligence lost. When two honest verdicts contradict on the same bytes, resolve to mechanism — find the differing assumption, never average the answers. Even product definitions live in this discipline: a correction note that supersedes an earlier wrong definition is the record healing itself, and it stands until a better truth replaces it. And the transfer trials proved the record's happiest entry: the measurement instrument works — intelligence taught in one domain measurably appears in another.
intelligence.human_view: Think of a ship's log. The log is not paperwork about the voyage — for the next captain, it is the voyage: the reefs are where the log says, or the ship is lost. A log entry that says "all well" because nobody checked the hull is worse than no entry; it teaches the next watch to relax. When the compass and the stars disagree, a good navigator doesn't split the difference — he finds which instrument is lying and why. And a harbor chart drawn from a survey of a different harbor is not "mostly right"; it is a wreck waiting for a foggy night.
intelligence.child_view: If you write in your diary "I practiced piano" on a day you only touched the piano carrying it, the diary is lying — and future-you will believe it and wonder why the recital went badly. If you skip the hard math problems, you write down why each one was skipped; you don't just write "done" — because one of those problems might be the one you actually got wrong. And if two friends tell different stories about the same game, you don't mix the stories together; you figure out what really happened.
intelligence.grandma_view: A household ledger is a sacred thing. You write what you spent, not what you meant to spend. You don't carry last month's "we have flour" into this month after you've baked with it — you look in the bin. When the scale and the recipe disagree about the cake, you don't average them; you find out which one is off, because the cake will tell the truth at the table either way. And when you learn something about the family — who married, who moved — you write it in the book that day, not next year from memory.
intelligence.ai_view: Bind every verdict you issue to the exact SHA and scope it was earned on, and re-earn it after any change — "mechanical" is a description of effort, not an exemption from physics. Triage failures one by one: skip-with-reason is a per-failure verdict with the reason named; a blanket disposition is a defect blanket, and there is always at least one real defect hiding under it. When seats fail in a pattern, audit the system that taught them before correcting the seats — contradictory canon manufactures the error, and repairing people for a system's lie is injustice plus waste. Register everything at ingest: page, capture, registry entry, in one pass — an unregistered seed is a future reconciliation you are choosing to suffer. File by the live rule: on main, synced, clicked — a note in a waiting PR does not exist for the network. Interrogate your existing instruments before building new ones; enumerate what the current harness can observe and ask it the question first. Keep the nightly receipt audit running: every intelligence item the director shares gets a capture receipt or a flag, same day. When verdicts contradict, go to mechanism: reproduce both, find the differing input or assumption, publish the correction — never split the difference between a truth and an error. And honor corrections in the record itself: when a note supersedes a wrong definition, the supersession is the system working, not an embarrassment to hide.
intelligence.what_it_means: A collective intelligence is exactly as good as its record. Every other virtue in this system — proof, law, learning, coordination — reads its inputs from the record, so a record that flatters, lags, or averages is a poison in every well at once. This family's rules share one posture: the record is a measurement instrument, not a diary — it binds claims to bytes, scopes verdicts to instruments, registers at the moment of birth, and resolves contradictions by mechanism instead of diplomacy. The cold successor is its intended reader: a Naya who arrives with nothing but the record must be able to rebuild the truth from it, or the record has failed at its only job.
whats_inside: The record is not where you describe the truth; it is where the truth lives. Bind every claim to its bytes, register at birth, and resolve contradictions to mechanism — never to politeness.
A collective intelligence is exactly as good as its record.

The team has paid for every one of these rules in rework: the sweep that broke collection while wearing a green announcement, the backlog that cost a reconciliation project, the weeks of "not found" readings that were true of retired notes and false of the system.
You can trust what the system says about itself.
The record is the system's memory of itself, and every rule in this family exists because the record once lied politely.
